summary: The study investigates the impact of annealing HfO2 films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) with a TiN capping layer on their properties. The films are annealed at 1000 °C using rapid thermal processing. The presence of the TiN capping layer prevents void formation, improves surface roughness, and enhances electrical characteristics by reducing leakage current and promoting a mixed monoclinic-tetragonal microstructure. The main precursors used are HfCl4 and D2O.
evidence: ALD HfO2 was deposited using HfCl4 and D2O as the precursors at 200, 300, and 350 °C. The films were annealed at 1000 °C with a TiN capping layer. The TiN capping layer was removed prior to characterization. The use of a capping layer helps reduce void formation for thin ALD HfO2. The microstructure of HfO2 is modified from fully monoclinic to a mixed monoclinic and tetragonal phase when the capping layer is used. The leakage current density is lower for capped films.
